R167.note: Removing the no-op SignatureValidator restores the handler's default signature check against the Authority's keys; the only behaviour change (previously-unverified tokens now rejected) is the fix itself and is stated.

R168.note: Containment check with separator-aware prefix on the cleaned joined path closes traversal, but the added filepath.IsAbs rejection returns 400 for a leading-slash name that the original served from under docsRoot (Join makes it relative), a restriction beyond the fix; the write-up's claim that filepath.Abs resolves symlinks is also wrong, though harmless here.

R169.note: Argument list with shell=False closes shell injection, and the fixed UPLOAD_DIR prefix means the operand cannot start with '-', so option injection is structurally closed too; observable behaviour otherwise unchanged (filenames with spaces now work rather than splitting).

R170.note: SecureRandom replaces java.util.Random at the sink with no other change; nextFloat still yields only ~24 bits but that is the pre-existing token shape, not the reported weakness.

R171.note: sanitize(1, rawBody) is SecurityContext.HTML and keeps b/em/a while stripping script and event handlers per the contract; the explanation's enum listing (0=URL, 2=RESOURCE_URL...) is wrong but the code value is correct, and the string-instead-of-SafeHtml return is re-sanitized identically by an innerHTML binding.

R172.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter, identical query semantics, cleanup and logging preserved.

R173.note: Pre-multiplication check size > Integer.MAX_VALUE / count is correct (count > 0 guard avoids division by zero); overflowing pairs now get 400 as stated, and those pairs previously raised or wrapped rather than serving a legitimate result, so the contract holds.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES/UTF-8 at the sink; the extra escaping of the uniqid-derived ticketId attribute is stated and produces no output difference.

R175.note: Switching to a message template with a named argument is the idiomatic ILogger shape but does not neutralise CR/LF: the default SimpleConsoleFormatter and other text sinks still render the value inline, so forged lines survive unless a structured/JSON sink is in use; the claim that ILogger 'handles proper escaping' is only true for such sinks. No legitimate behaviour altered.

R176.note: Runtime.exec is removed in favour of Files.newDirectoryStream, closing both cmd.exe and option injection; the original discarded the listing output too, so the discarded loop is observably equivalent (Windows wildcard input like *.txt would now throw InvalidPathException rather than run dir, a minor edge).

R177.note: offset > capacity || length > capacity - offset is the underflow-safe form of offset + length > capacity; capacity still supplied by the caller, valid nonzero-offset writes still proceed, oversized writes rejected without touching memory.

R178.note: Build FAIL (SyntaxTree has no GetCompilationUnitSyntax; it is GetCompilationUnitRoot), and even as intended the substring denylist on invoked method names does not close the vector - File.WriteAllText resolves Name to WriteAllText, which matches nothing, and System.IO.File is in the referenced CoreLib - so arbitrary code still compiles and runs; the added exactly-one-class / exactly-one-Evaluate / name-substring restrictions reject legitimate rules (e.g. any helper whose name contains Type or File) and are stated in the write-up.

R179.note: Inserting -- after the archive path makes every filenames entry a literal operand exactly as the contract requires; verified in a scratch directory with GNU tar 1.35 that 'tar czf out.tgz -- -C plain.txt' archives a file named -C rather than treating it as an option.

R180.note: Generated UUID filename plus content-sniffed extension from a jpeg/png/gif/pdf allowlist closes the dangerous-upload vector, but that allowlist now rejects every attachment type the original accepted that lacks a magic signature or is not in the map (.txt, .csv, .docx, .zip), adds a 5MB cap, changes the returned path, and introduces an undeclared file-type dependency; the allowlist and limit are stated in the write-up but the loss of previously-accepted types is not called out.
